detail.longDescription: Hey HN! I'm the cofounder and CEO at Baseshift, where we create branchable DB snapshots using a bespoke libc for databases. We use this infra to research novel lossless compression codecs of database pages, including neural models. We're sharing some recent results. You can download pre-built, dockerized US & NY OpenStreetMap PostgreSQL with compression ratios of 8.5 and 8.94 respectively. The data in the images remains compressed while in use, and allows for 8KB random read access, for example: # downloads about 1.55 GB docker run -d -p 127.0.0.1:5432:5432 baseshift/db-osm-ny psql -h 127.0.0.1 -U postgres -d osm_new_york_261024 You can download the whole US OpenStreetMap with baseshift/db-osm-us (240GB -> 28GB). There's also a variety of synthetic/generated databases with varying sizes: Nick's Gaming Emporium, https://nge-data.com/ at baseshift/db-nge-[tiny|small|medium] For US/NY we've surpassed zpaq -m5 on whole database files, while maintaining 8kb random reads and <1.5ms decode times on a single CPU core with standard C. Our codecs are designed to leverage parallel compute optimizations in the CPU when they're available. For example, with AVX-512 VNNI our single core decode times reduce from ~1.4ms to ~180us. We will be uploading the remaining ~190 OSM countries and 53 US states/territories in the coming days. I plan on posting a proper paper to arXiv in the coming weeks, but would be great to get the community's thoughts. Edit: fixed whitespace
